thread:
anya: Heads up — noticed a perf regression in nightly 2.1.4 for MQA workloads when seqlen crosses ~96->128 on paged-KV setups. Throughput drops ~18% and latency p95 spikes.

ravi: ugh, which kernel path is it falling back to? GQA or some paged-attn fallback?

anya: It's flipping between the small-block paged-attn kernel and the generic tiled-attn kernel. The autotuner is oscillating at the 96-128 boundary and ends up picking the slower tiled path half the time.

samir: can you paste the profiler output? quick flamegraph or nvprof snippet would help.

anya: here's a short dump from perf-bot run (trimmed):
```
perf-bot: run=nightly-2368, model=gpt-13b-mqa, hw=A100-40GB
seqlen=120, batch=8, tokens/sec=22.6k, p95=143ms
chosen-kernel=pagedsmall_block_sz=64 (30% of requests)
chosen-kernel=tiled_attn (70% of requests)
gpu-cycles: tiled_attn >> pagedsmall (varies)
kernel-switch-overhead ~= 5.8ms/request when paths alternate
```

lina: that kernel-switch overhead screams hysteresis problem. autotuner is too eager when seqlen jitter crosses bracket edges.

ravi: agree. We should add a sequence-length hysteresis window and also a min-request-count threshold before switching. current autotuner uses only median-seqlen per minute.

anya: posted a repro script (local):
```bash
# repro loop: vary seqlen between 96..136 to trigger oscillation
for L in 96 112 120 128 136; do 
  ./bench_client --model gpt-13b-mqa --seq_len $L --batch 8 --requests 200 
done
```

samir: running that now on a dev node. also toggled paged-block-size to 128/256 to see fragmentation impact. early note: blocksize=256 reduces kernel switches but increases mem copies for small seqs.

perf-bot: automated analysis attached to thread: 
- regression_window: 2026-02-12T03:12:00Z..2026-02-12T05:00:00Z
- affected_models: [gpt-6b-mqa, gpt-13b-mqa]
- seqlen_brackets_hit: {64-96: 40%, 96-128: 52%, 128-192: 8%}
- avg_kernel_select_time: 0.52ms -> 0.83ms when oscillating

ravi: proposed config for autotuner hysteresis (pseudo):
```json
{
  "kernel_picker": {
    "seqlen_brackets": [64, 96, 128, 192],
    "switch_hysteresis_ms": 1200,
    "min_samples_before_switch": 150,
    "prefer_stable_kernel_for_small_batches": true
  }
}
```

lina: also to note: KV-stripe fragmentation shows up when blocksize mismatches common prefix lengths. we should emit a metric: kvcache.fragmentation_ratio by model+blocksize so ops can correlate.

anya: agreed. I pushed a small patch that: 1) adds hysteresis_ms, 2) increments a per-model switch counter, 3) emits kvcache.fragmentation_ratio. Diff inline: 
```diff
+ if (candidate != current && time_since_last_switch > hysteresis_ms && samples >= min_samples) {
+   current = candidate;
+ }
```

samir: running canary with that patch + blocksize=128 on dedicated dev pool. starting 30m workload now. will report throughput/latency delta.

ravi: also consider a micro-optim: when kernels are compatible, keep the same kernels but switch internal parameters (tile size) instead of switching full kernel binary. reduces launch overhead. put on backlog if not quick.

lina: scheduling a follow-up benchmark: vary batch sizes [1,4,8,16] x seqlens [64,96,120,128,160] and collect kernel-switch counts + p95. I put a tracker in the perf board.

anya: thanks — if canary looks good we'll roll to nightly and monitor kvcache.fragmentation_ratio and kernel_switches metrics. tagging @ravi for code review. :thumbsup:

ravi: reviewing now, will approve if numbers look clean.

perf-bot: canary results (30m): throughput delta +2.1% avg, kernel_switch_count -78%, p95 down 12ms for seqlen 96-128 bracket.

anya: awesome. I'll coordinate a staged rollout tomorrow. leaving notes in the PR about blocksize tradeoffs and the memory copy cost for 256.

samir: thanks — saved the repro artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/repro/2368001111 for anyone who wants to replay.

lina: added dashboard tiles for kvcache.fragmentation_ratio and kernel_switch_count. will watch first 24h. :eyes:
